title: Respect your shame
line: Five days meeting each slip with three sentences, not self-punishment.
intro: The Delphic maxim αἰσχύνην σέβου, “respect shame”, is Athena’s healthy alternative to self-flagellation: shame is justice regulating itself in you, and feeling it is healthy. Respecting it means seeing the error, learning, adjusting and moving on. For five days, each time you slip, you answer with the same three sentences.
does: For five days, meet each slip with Athena’s three sentences, adjust, and let it go.
trains: A healthy dialogue with conscience in place of self-punishment.
each: Whenever something goes wrong today (a sharp word, a promise broken, a small lie to yourself), pause and say, silently or aloud: “I’m human, I erred, I deceived myself here. What can I learn?” Then make one small adjustment, an apology or a change, and let it go. No going over it again at night.
note: Where did you slip today, if at all, what did you learn, and could you let it go?
end: After five days, how is meeting a slip with these three sentences different from the way you usually treat yourself?
